title: Remote forward port allocator starts at a fixed 47000 and never reserves or probes, so tests and concurrent hosts collide with a live tunnel
outcome: Remote forward port allocator starts at a fixed 47000 and never reserves or probes, so tests and concurrent hosts collide with a live tunnel
acceptance: Remote forward port selection reserves or probes a free loopback port (or uses an OS-assigned port) instead of incrementing from a fixed 47000 without checking, and a busy port leads to another choice or a typed error, never a silent masked failure.

Tests that start fake or real forwards never collide with a live TermAl host's tunnels on the same machine; a regression test holds 47000 (and the next ports) open and shows allocation still succeeds.
Exact-input focused tests, the full five-stage gate and an independent review pair with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
